contentText:
Argentine duo CA7RIEL and Paco Amoroso sit down at Planta Queen in New York City for an unforgettable lunch interview. The two open up about their new album, Free Spirits , their Grammy-winning year, their dramatic “We Quit” announcement and how spending time with Sting completely transformed their lives. They also share wild stories from their 60-date world tour, their first time playing New York’s Bowery Ballroom and their upcoming show at Radio City Music Hall.

Plus, they discuss the story behind their collab with Anderson .Paak, Jack Black showing up as a baby in their music video, a hilarious cut song about a Nintendo Switch addiction and why they call themselves “throat actors.”

Isabela Raygoza: Eeeeh! Eeeeh! Welcome to New York! How are you?

CA7RIEL: Hi, my love! How are you? Everything good?

Isabela Raygoza: Yes, very good. All ready hungry, right?

CA7RIEL: Oof! I’m so hungry.

Isabela Raygoza: Yes, for the vegan life. Here we are at Planta in Queen.

Paco Amoroso: We are ready.

Isabela Raygoza: Yeah, all right. Prepare it. Let’s do it. Hi, I’m Isabela Raygoza, editor of Billboard Español , and I have the pleasure of being here with CA7RIEL and Paco Amoroso. What’s up, how are you? Welcome to New York.

Paco Amoroso: Thank you. We love being here.

Isabela Raygoza: And you’re visiting us directly from Argentina, right? What you were saying, that you traveled right now to be here.

Paco Amoroso: We traveled to be here. Certain commitments we have with … companies of all kinds. And also to talk to you a bit about Free Spirits . Talk to you about how we’re doing and, well, eat some tasty things.

Isabela Raygoza: And why Planta Queen?

Paco Amoroso: I think people sometimes think that we’re vegan and we no longer, we don’t question anything anymore.

Isabela Raygoza: Well, since you already have a cleanse, you got rid of all the … the chaos, all the, the partying. You arrived well …

CA7RIEL: One tries. Sometimes you can’t. You have to live with your demons, your urge to go out, your urge to break things. You can’t go around breaking things all the time, because they’re very expensive.

Isabela Raygoza: That’s right, it costs us a lot of money, right? Sometimes. Especially if we like the things.

Keep watching for more!
